result.summary: This pull request enables the `clang-analyzer-optin.performance.Padding` check in clang-tidy with an explicit threshold of 24 bytes to catch struct padding regressions. It reorders member variables across several internal data structures—including `CBlockIndex`, `CNode`, `CConnman`, `CTxMemPool`, `CWalletTx`, `Peer`, and `CRPCConvertParam`—to bring their padding below this limit.
result.problem: Suboptimal member ordering in long-lived or frequently allocated classes introduces unnecessary padding and wasted memory. Without automated tooling, new struct members can introduce padding inefficiencies unnoticed.
evidence: Commit c2dedba48f notes that reordering CBlockIndex on Windows x64 saves 8 bytes per instance, saving ~8MB of RAM for a 1M block height.
PR description states the check is added to catch padding regressions above the 24-byte default threshold.
result.scope_notes: This RFC combines tooling configuration with struct layout refactors across networking, mempool, chain, RPC, and wallet classes.
result.card: This PR enables clang-tidy's optin.performance.Padding check with a 24-byte threshold and reorders member variables in CBlockIndex, CNode, CConnman, CTxMemPool, CWalletTx, Peer, and CRPCConvertParam to eliminate existing padding warnings. The change aims to reduce memory usage in long-lived structures and catch future struct padding regressions. The commit message cites roughly 8MB in RAM savings from the CBlockIndex layout changes at 1M blocks. It is an RFC based on and including #36501.

risk.why: Reordering member variables across core networking, mempool, and validation classes could lead to uninitialized reads if constructor initialization lists do not match declaration order.
